target_customer: Clinics, health workers and public health programs in emerging markets that lack lab access
problem: Diagnosing infectious disease usually needs specialized labs and costs over 10 USD per test. Unima built fast low-cost rapid tests for use at the point of care.
business_model: Diagnostic test kits sold to clinics and health programs, with disease surveillance data

founders.name: Laura Mendoza
previous_startups: Custovac, a vaccine stabilizer sold in 14 countries

founders.name: Jose Luis Nuno Ayala
founders.background_notes: Named by the LAVCA interview as co-founder and brother of Alejandro and Rodrigo. Not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Rodrigo Nuno
founders.role: Founder, head of manufacturing then Director of Engineering

technical_complexity.rationale: Developing paper-strip antibody tests using shark-derived VNAR antibodies, with clinical trials and regulatory approval needed, is research-grade work for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: The antibody technology and the need for regulatory approvals made copying slow, though rapid test incumbents existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition found. A 2023 TechCrunch article says the team later built Narval from the same VNAR work.

market_need_then: The LAVCA interview says existing diagnostics need specialized labs and cost above 10 USD per test, leaving about three billion people underserved. At YC Winter 2016 Demo Day the product was pitched as a 1 USD paper strip with 15 minute results for HIV and tuberculosis first.

branding.domain_note: Used unimadx.com, a prefix and suffix variant. Dates not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: mission driven, health access in emerging markets

branding.brand_signature: Find, the rapid testing platform name
branding.community_and_virality: Won the 2018 WeXchange pitch competition and was named in a 2018 Forbes list of women-led startups.

brand_strength.rationale: Some press and pitch competition wins, but no evidence that the brand itself drove growth.

pivots.why: YC page says the company shifted to diagnostics. The reason is not stated.

outcome_analysis: Unima raised about 2.6 million USD by 2019 from Mexican and international investors and won a 2018 pitch competition while developing a tuberculosis test and running clinical and regulatory work. The YC page lists it as inactive, but CB Insights lists it as alive, and a 2023 TechCrunch piece says the team's later startup Narval grew from this work. No public shutdown cause was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty.
notes: Funding totals conflict across aggregators (CB Insights 120K, Bouncewatch 2.02M, StartupBlink 3.7M); the LAVCA interview figures (2.6M total, about 2M equity and 600K grants) are company stated and undated, so round dates are null. An ITU 2020 slide deck reportedly lists a 2M seed and 450K grants but its text could not be read. Status conflict: YC says inactive, CB Insights says alive. No dated competitor source near the batch was found, so the list is empty. The company website returned 403.
